name: Mailisu (麦丽素)
blurb: Chocolate-coated malt balls, China's local take on Maltesers, sold since the 1980s
title: What Is Mailisu (麦丽素)? China's Chocolate Malt Ball Snack
description: Mailisu (麦丽素) are chocolate-coated malt balls modelled on Mars's Maltesers, made in China since the 1980s and a childhood favourite. Still made today.
answer: Mailisu (麦丽素) is a Chinese chocolate malt ball: a thin chocolate shell around a light, crunchy malted centre, each about the size of a fingertip. It is modelled on Maltesers, which Mars created in 1936, and Chinese factories began making it in the 1980s. Through the late 1980s and 1990s it was one of the most common chocolate treats in corner shops, and it is still made today by Chinese companies such as Jiangsu Liangfeng.

sections.h: What it looks and tastes like
body: Each piece is a small brown ball. Bite through the chocolate and you reach a pale, honeycomb-like malt centre full of tiny air pockets, with a milky, malty taste close to malted milk drinks. It feels lighter and crunchier than a solid chocolate bean.

Many Chinese versions used a cocoa butter substitute in the coating, which made it sweeter and slower to melt than imported chocolate. That is part of why people who grew up with it say mailisu tastes like mailisu, not like Maltesers. Today makers sell both cocoa-butter-substitute and real cocoa butter versions, and the ingredient list tells you which one you have.
The model was Maltesers: created in 1936 by Forrest Mars Sr. at the Mars factory in Slough, England, and first sold in 1937. Maltesers is still a Mars brand.

In the 1980s, Chinese food factories began producing their own version and called it 麦丽素, usually explained as a transliteration of the English name Mylikes. Who coined the name is not settled: some accounts credit a Hong Kong brand, others the Liangfeng food company in Zhangjiagang, Jiangsu. Liangfeng's version is often said to have gone into production in 1986, and the company's own history says its Mailisu milk chocolate won a national light-industry quality award in 1987. Many other factories followed, so the name became a generic word for this kind of snack.

body: Yes. Mailisu was never discontinued. Jiangsu Liangfeng Food Group and other Chinese makers still produce it in bags of various sizes, in both the classic coating and a real cocoa butter version. Maltesers is a separate product from a different company, with its own recipe.

faq.q: Is mailisu the same as Maltesers?
faq.a: Same idea, different product. Maltesers is a Mars brand created in 1936; mailisu is the Chinese version made by local companies since the 1980s, each with its own recipe.
It is usually explained as a transliteration of Mylikes; the first character, mai, also means wheat or malt. Which company coined it is disputed.
No. Liangfeng and other Chinese makers still produce it.
